quotes.text: Chat is stateless by design. Every turn is independent. You ask, it responds done. But agents don't work that way. Agents require state. They need memory across sessions.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains in a few lines why the chat paradigm is the wrong abstraction for agents.

quotes.text: An agent without an identity is a ghost. You can't audit it. You can't control it. You can't govern it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable case for giving every agent its own identity instead of shared service accounts.

quotes.text: Deleting isn't the same as forgetting. If information is baked into a vector embedding or a graph structure, deleting the raw text isn't enough.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Highlights a hard compliance problem with persistent agent memory.

quotes.text: We have to stop treating DLP as an external enforcement tool and start treating it as a design constraint.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes data loss prevention for multi-agent systems where data moves between agents at machine speed.

quotes.text: Instead of trying to prevent a compromise which is nearly impossible at scale, we contain the damage when it happens.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the shift from detection to containment in agent security.

chapters.title: The silo problem and why chat is wrong

takeaways: Enterprise agents fail not because models are weak but because they are built as stateless, siloed chat interfaces instead of persistent system participants.
A working agent fabric needs session persistence, a shared backend with thin clients, a dedicated Entra Agent ID per agent, explicit orchestration and model routing to control cost.
Persistent memory and agent-to-agent calls create new risks such as memory poisoning and data leakage, which require Agent 365 governance, DLP by design, sandboxing and causal observability.
hook: Most organizations think they have AI agents, but what they really have are chatbots that forget everything when the window closes. This episode is for architects and IT leaders planning enterprise agents on the Microsoft stack. It lays out the agent fabric blueprint, from GitHub Copilot SDK session persistence to Entra Agent IDs, orchestration, cost routing and Agent 365 governance.
